title: arxiv_2603.17866v3
universal_lens: A Bayesian multilevel generative model for player movement evaluates observed trajectories against hypothetical alternatives using step length and turn angle distributions. Bayesian hypothetical comparison of player movement through generative simulation and empirical validation.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive inference on step-and-turn models to assess player performance through posterior predictive simulations, enabling robust valuation under uncertainty. {'gsi_mapping': 'The sovereign primitive maps to GSI through a hierarchical Bayesian copula framework, where empirical tracking data features are embedded within multivariate von Mises-Gaussian distributions. This enables conformal predictive intervals for future step-length and turn-angle trajectories, supporting rigorous statistical inference on player performance and defensive coordination.'}
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes state-transition kernels derived from step-and-turn dynamics to simulate plausible next-step behaviors, supporting tactical decision-making in real-time gameplay scenarios. {'gse_mapping': 'The sovereign primitive provides GSE with a state-transition kernel for situational reasoning, where the current position and velocity vector serve as latent state variables. The predicted joint distribution of step length and turn angle informs optimal decision-making under uncertainty, while accounting for opponent-player interactions and dynamic field configurations.'}

primitives.name: Step-and-Turn Generative Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Specifically, we develop Bayesian multilevel models for frame-level player movement based on two components: step length (distance between successive locations) and turn angle (change in direction between successive steps).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_t': 'step length at time t (meters)', 'θ_t': 'turn angle at time t (radians)', 'y_t': 'player position at time t (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player movement follows a stochastic process with spatial dependencies; step lengths and turn angles are conditionally independent given prior positions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When step length approaches zero or turn angle exceeds π radians, model degenerates into deterministic or highly erratic motion.

layer2.mapping: The step-and-turn kernel defines local probabilistic transitions in player state space, enabling GSE to simulate alternative movement paths while preserving empirical constraints from tracking data.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior predictive p-values for observed vs. simulated step lengths and turn angles

primitives.name: Posterior Predictive Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using the step-and-turn models, we perform posterior predictive simulation to generate hypothetical ball carrier steps at each frame during a play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y_{obs}^t': 'observed player position at frame t (meters)', 'y_{sim}^t': 'simulated player position at frame t (meters)', 'p(y_{sim}^t | y_{obs}^{1:t-1})': 'predictive distribution over simulated positions'}
primitives.assumptions: Simulations are generated conditional on observed history and model parameters; uncertainty is propagated through hierarchical structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If observed trajectory deviates significantly from model support, predictive distributions become diffuse or invalid.

layer2.mapping: Posterior predictive simulations mirror GSI's use of Bayesian calibration for generating synthetic datasets that match empirical moments.
layer2.telemetry: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test statistic comparing empirical and simulated step/angle distributions

primitives.name: Von Mises Concentration Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: We fit the following multilevel model for φijt: φijt ∼von Mises(μ(TA) ijt , κijt), tan μ(TA) ijt 2 = α(TA) 0 + X(TA) ijt β(TA), log κijt = γ0 + γ1sijt + wj, wj ∼N(0, τ 2 w).

primitives.assumptions: Circular normality of turn angles, log-linear dependence of concentration on step length, additive fixed effects for tracking features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degeneracy when κ_ijt → 0 (uniform distribution) or κ_ijt → ∞ (point mass), requiring γ0 + γ1 s_ijt > 0.

layer2.mapping: Realizes GSE state-transition matrices with row-stochastic von Mises kernels, where concentration modulates diffusion rate and drift encodes directional bias.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical metric: Mean resultant length of turn angles, serving as proxy for maneuverability sharpness.
